correctness.rationale: The local five-bit composition gives a 16-state transfer for the exact two-update map. Direct checking of 32 windows yields the complete row table of T_0 T_1. Its closed walks avoid transient or dead states; the surviving seven vertices admit a four-class reduction in which every allowed class transition has exactly one target vertex, giving a bijection of closed walks. The four-class adjacency K has det(I-zK)=1-z-2z^2-2z^3-z^4, and the standard logarithmic derivative identity yields the claimed recurrence and generating function for all m>=1. The constant-output cases follow by classifying fixed all-zero and all-one preimages of Rule 50. The included checker verifies the nonstandard row reduction and determinant and directly enumerates every input at the stated finite lengths; those experiments are not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The question exhaustively classifies inverse fibers over a naturally defined periodic-output subsystem (all targets of period dividing two) after a nontrivial second iterate. The checkerboard branch has a genuinely four-state transfer representation, exact quartic recurrence and sharp Perron growth, yielding an explicit nontrivial two-step output probability. Unlike a small table or an arbitrary index slice, the family is complete for the simplest nonconstant periodic output and its length varies without bound. This provides an exact benchmark for finite-ring inverse-branching and higher-iterate studies without overstating global optimality.
